text: Which of the following statements regarding amyloidosis is/are correct? Amyloidosis is characterized by the extracellular deposition of abnormal protein fibrils that interfere with normal tissue function. Congo red staining under polarized light reveals a characteristic apple-green birefringence, which is considered diagnostic for amyloid deposits. X-ray crystallography can detect the presence of beta-pleated sheet conformations, which are a hallmark of amyloid fibrils. The primary form of amyloidosis, known as AL amyloidosis, occurs due to an accumulation of amyloid deposits secondary to chronic inflammation. The extracellular amyloid deposits primarily consist of misfolded proteins that accumulate within cells, leading to organ dysfunction.

text: A 72-year-old man undergoes coronary artery bypass graft for severe coronary artery disease. He is extubated on the second postoperative day. On the third postoperative day he complains of dyspnea and worsening retrosternal pain despite continuous analgesia with morphine. His temperature is 38.6° C , blood pressure is 112/52 mm Hg, pulse is 125/min and irregularly irregular and respirations are 28/min. Examination shows normal heart sounds. A small amount of cloudy fluid is present in the sternal wound drain. His ECG shows atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. An x-ray film of the chest shows widening of the mediastinum. Echocardiography reveals a small amount of pericardial fluid. Laboratory studies show Hemoglobin 8.9 mg/L WBC Count 16,300/mm3 Which of the following will this patient most likely require?

text: A young weight lifting aspirant was making his way through the higher leagues in weight lifting contest, through his vigorous training sessions. He is eyeing for the gold medal in the upcoming Olympics. He underwent constant training to achieve his goal. Initially he had symptoms of regurgitation and heart burn occasionally. But he ignored them and still pursued his training sessions. During a training session, he increased the weights, where after lifting, he felt a severe chest pain radiating to the back. After few minutes he developed dyspnea, that is when he was brought to the emergency bay. ECG was normal. Chest X-ray reveal air in the mediastinum. At this time, what will be the diagnosis ?
